newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks muddle through, close lower.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks muddle through, close lower.

text.p: Chilean stocks took their cue from Wall Street and stagnated through the day, ending about half a point lower despite strong outlooks for third quarter earnings reports this week.

The blue-chip IPSA index fell below the psychological 100-point barrier, ending 0.5 percent lower to 99.71 points, in what brokers described as a dispiriting session of few orders, soft prices and desultory trading.
"The market is dry and people are in a wait-and-see pattern," said one broker, adding that he did not expect any general recovery this week.
Moody's issued a debt-rating report on Santander and three other banks, but brokers said the drop was not necessarily a result of the report.

Chilgener wobbled through the day and ended off about 0.9 percent at 2420 pesos, partly on lower earnings at its part-owned Central Puerto de Argentina. Brokers reported good expectations for Chilgener's third quarter earnings report, to be issued Tuesday at 0900 local time/1200 GMT.
Gainers included Banco de Chile's B series, up 1.3 percent to 26.6 pesos, and winery Santa Rita, up 1.3 to 57.5 pesos.
The all-share IGPA index ended 0.20 percent lower to 5432.52 points on paltry volume of 110 million shares traded.
Investors were reluctant to stake out positions until the government publishes electricity rates, expected in early November, which will affect electrical share, brokers said.
Losers included Colbun, the state power utility slated for partial privatization, which fell from last week's highs to end 2.8 percent lower at 43.5 pesos.
Calichera was off 2.8 percent to 190 pesos, and Banco Santander-Chile slipped 0.9 percent to 26.25 pesos in high volume.
Soquimich rose 0.9 percent to 2300 pesos on expectations of strong third quater earnings, brokers said.
Chilean companies have until Wednesday to report their third quarter earnings.
